issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/NaN inputs to 0 instead of propagating NaN as the prior toNumber path did
issues.detail: Original panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber, returning null for non-numeric input and propagating NaN downstream. The new coerceNumber uses `?? 0`, complecting coercion with a default and changing observable values under a 'just added types' claim. Either preserve NaN-propagation or document the policy change explicitly.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the isNonEmpty guard fires, defeating the empty-domain invariant
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) runs in panLog/zoomLog before delegating to pan/zoom, so empty input yields Math.sign(undefined) = NaN before the error throws. The non-empty precondition is asserted in the wrong place. Hoist the check to each public entry point so the invariant holds once at the boundary.

issues.description: Public domain parameter typed as number[] when the code actually requires NonEmptyArray<number>
issues.detail: isNonEmpty narrows inside but signatures still advertise number[]. Declaring NonEmptyArray<number> on the boundary would make the precondition checkable by typed callers at compile time, leaving the runtime throw as a real backstop. Half-typed is worse than fully typed.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is a policy change smuggled into a typing refactor without tests for most entry points
issues.detail: The PR claims same runtime behavior but adds a throw; downstream callers relying on NaN propagation are affected. Tests cover only panLinear/zoomLinear, leaving panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog unproved for the new error path. Separate the policy change and broaden coverage.

issues.description: Local identity shadows the existing accessors.identity import without justification
issues.detail: The old file imported identity from './accessors.js'; the new file defines a local typed identity and drops the import. Functionally equivalent but diverges from codebase voice and duplicates a shared utility. Either reuse the import or add a one-line comment explaining the narrower-typed local.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. Two P1 issues land with full consensus: coerceNumber silently swaps toNumber's null-returning behavior for 0-coercion (a runtime semantics change buried in a typing PR), and panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the empty-domain guard runs, so the new invariant fails for the very functions that need it most. Beyond those, the public number[] type understates the required NonEmptyArray<number> precondition, the empty-domain throw is a policy change with tests covering only two of eight entry points, and a local identity needlessly shadows the shared accessors utility. Fix the coercion semantics, hoist the non-empty check to the public boundary, and either tighten the input type or broaden the tests before merge.
